MRK.rationale: Merck's Q1 2026 results reveal a severe earnings collapse: net income swung to -$4.24B (EPS -$1.72) from +$5.79B in Q3 2025, driven by a massive operating loss of -$3.53B despite revenue of $16.29B. This is not a one-quarter blip—the company's net margin has halved from ~29% to 13.6%, and ROE has collapsed from ~37% to 19.5%. Meanwhile, the stock has rallied 55% from its 52-week low of $76.66 to $129.56, pushing the P/E to 35.8x—more than triple its 12-month low of 11.1x and at the absolute top of its 365-day range. The market is paying a premium multiple for a business whose earnings power has deteriorated sharply. The Keytruda patent cliff (2028-2029) looms as the dominant structural risk, with 46% of 2024 revenue concentrated in a single drug facing imminent loss of exclusivity. Gardasil demand is declining in China and Japan. Recent pipeline setbacks (EVOKE-03 discontinuation, LITESPARK-012 missing endpoints) undermine the narrative that new launches can replace Keytruda. CMS proposed drug price negotiations starting 2029 add regulatory headwinds. The combination of deteriorating fundamentals, extreme valuation vs. own history, and no credible near-term catalyst to reverse the earnings trajectory makes this strongly unattractive. The Q2 2026 earnings call on Aug 4 is more likely to confirm weakness than catalyze a re-rating.
